page: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is a high-density, compute-oriented virtual machine configured with 192 vCPUs across 96 dedicated physical cores. Powered by the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance integrates a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512 vector acceleration. The system allocates 384 GB of system memory, providing a lean ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and bundles 11,340 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute efficiency. In multi-core stress testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 202,853.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 152,145.2, both ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. High-bandwidth memory performance reached 688.55 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 270.97 GB/sec on writes, which paired with local NVMe storage to sustain 268.62 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 157.94 GB/sec in static web throughput. Single-core execution on stress-ng placed in the average tier at 2,289.99, while single-threaded compression tests remained strong.

Tradeoffs center around memory capacity per core and specific text generation characteristics. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers high compute density per dollar for execution-heavy workloads, but it restricts utilization in memory-intensive in-memory databases requiring higher RAM allocations. Furthermore, while prompt processing throughput on large language models remains strong due to vector and matrix instruction support, sequential text generation throughput is modest without discrete GPU hardware.

The D192lds_v7 is suited for massive parallel workloads, large-scale software compilation, distributed caching, high-throughput static web delivery, batch compression pipelines, and database operations benefiting directly from high-capacity local NVMe storage.

Designed with a 1:2 memory ratio, the configuration provides 384 GB of RAM and 11,340 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. In empirical testing, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute performance and high memory bandwidth, achieving over 202,000 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 268 million Redis SET operations per second. This instance is well matched for distributed caching, high-volume batch processing, data compression pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving workloads.
